security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's vsetvl helper (vector_helper.c:82-83) validates fractional LMUL via the constraint 'ELEN >> (8 - vlmul) < sew', which checks ELEN*LMUL >= SEW. This is the OLD spec constraint (LMUL >= SEW_MIN/ELEN). The updated spec replaces this with LMUL >= SEW_MIN/VLEN, meaning e8mf8 is valid when VLEN>=64 regardless of ELEN. On configurations with ELEN=32 and VLEN>=64 (e.g., VLEN=128), QEMU spuriously sets vill=1 for vtype encodings with e32mf2 (vlmul=5, sew=32), e16mf4 (vlmul=6, sew=16), and e8mf8 (vlmul=5, sew=8) because 32 >> 3 = 4 < sew. Under the new spec, VLEN=128 >> 3 = 16 ≥ 8, so 1/8 LMUL provides ≥8 bits for an element and these configurations are valid.
security_spec.summary: Fractional LMUL vill-setting uses ELEN-based floor instead of VLEN-based floor, causing spurious illegal-instruction traps for valid vector type configurations (e32mf2, e16mf4, e8mf8) when ELEN=32 and VLEN>=64
